Commentary.Commentary: Taijul Islam starred with the ball for his side with a 5-fer, while Mehidy Hasan bagged 3 and Nazmul Islam got 2. So, winning this Test match for Bangladesh is a monumental task to say the least, so the approach has to be a step-by-step one. The first one will be to see the day out without much damage. And then, take it from there. Don't go anywhere, the final innings will begin shortly.

So the hosts bundle up the visitors and have 321 runs to chase down and win this Test. After gaining a lead of 139 runs, Zimbabwe were firmly in control of this match. They batted without much pressure and kept the runs coming. Wickets kept falling at regular intervals, but some handy contributions from Hamilton Masakadza and the rest saw them post a huge target on the board.

OUT! Bangladesh have wrapped things up here. Taijul Islam plucks the final wicket. Bowls the arm ball on middle, it keeps coming in with the angle. Chatara goes back to play at it but he doesn't expect the ball to come at such pace. Gets rapped on the back pad and the finger goes up. Tendai, for the sake of it, reviews it and it's taken upstairs. Replays show it's pad first, then bat, so he's out of here. ZIMBABWE ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 181 AND SET A TARGET OF 321!
Review! Do Bangladesh have their final wicket? Chatara is caught leg before and given out. He's taken the DRS. Only thing that can save him is if it's bat first. Let's see here...
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Tendai Chatara. A similar kind of ball, Chatara plays a similar shot. Gets low and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket, beating the man in the deep. Super shot.
FOUR! Chatara not holding back here. Fuller, not much straight on it and in the slot. Chatara goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it aerially through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full and straight, on the stumps, pushed back down the track from inside the crease.

Ideal target would be between 350-375. Join us at 1500 local (0900 GMT) for the final session. Just 30 overs left in the day.

... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Wickets, wickets, wickets. And in clusters. That is what can bring Bangladesh back into the game. They are trying to slow down the proceedings but that has not helped them a big deal so far. Another decent session for the tourists might see the lead cross 300. Can the hosts produce what happened after Day 2, Lunch? Join us back at 12.40 pm local (0640 GMT).

Hamilton Masakadza has been soaking up all the pressure at one end while Brendan Taylor tried to get some quick runs. Eventually, the first hour was a watchful one, while the second was compensating for the sluggish hour.

Gets the sweep shot and directs the ball towards backward square leg for a single.

A bit of excitement. Flighted on off, Masakadza jumps down the track and looks to flick but gets a thick inside edge onto his boot. The ball lobs up and first slip thinks he has a chance to catch but cannot get there. Replays show that the ball bounced before it hit the boot.
Landed on middle, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Masakadza lunges to defend but the ball just about beats the outside edge.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
A touch short, punched towards mid on who is neither at the conventional position nor at long on. Somewhere in middle.
Landed outside off, spinning in, Chari goes back and punches it towards the bowler.
Comes forward and drives it towards long on for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
First bowling change of the morning. Mehidy Hasan is introduced, giving Jayed a break.
Full again, blocked towards cover.
Full and just around off, pushed back. past silly point.
Going straight on, just outside off, pushed towards cover.
Landed outside off, spinning away, watchfully left alone.
Full and just outside off, Hamilton gets a good stride forward to push it past slip for a run. Played that with soft hands.

Full and outside off, Chari drives it towards cover who misfields and parries it towards mid off. The striker senses an opportunity and calls his partner through for a quick single. Masakadza was not alert and had to hurry but made it in time. First run of Taijul this morning. In his 4th over for the day
Short leg being installed now. And a silly point is complimentary too.
Full and outside off, swinging in, another forward press, towards mid off. Consecutive maidens for Bangladesh.
Around off, solidly defended.

On a good length in the corridor of uncertainty but nothing uncertain about Hamilton's forward defense. Perfect placement of the front foot, right to the pitch of the ball and then getting the bat down to defend, with no gap between bat and pad.
Plenty of movement, from outside off, coming in, Masakadza plays that a bit loosely and the bottom hand comes off the bat. The ball goes off the inner half towards short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, driven towards mid on.
On a length outside off, punched towards point.

That is a beauty. Drew him forward and beat him all ends up. Full and outside off, a bit of flight, Chari lunges to defend but the ball turns away just that wee little bit to beat the outside edge. Third successive maiden for Taijul.
Darts this on middle, watchfully pushed towards point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A tad short, punched towards cover.
This is outside off, spinning away, left alone.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.

FOUR! Drifting down leg and pays the price. Just about releases the pressure being built with 16 dot balls on the trot. The lead moves to 153. Full and on the pads, easy pickings and Masakadza will not miss out on that. Flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Very full, around middle, Hamilton is nearly beaten as he initially attempts to flick but then, at the last moment, he adjusts and pushes the ball towards the bowler.
Landed outside off, on a length, pushed towards point.
Keeping it full and straight, Masakadza is upto the task and blocks it out.
Fuller and straighter, pushed back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, punched towards cover-point.
Much better. Comes forward, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it towards point.
Goes back again, committing the same mistake of playing on the back foot on this wearing pitch. Punches the ball back to the bowler.
THAT STAYS LOW. Pitched around middle, the arm ball, Chari goes back and tries to punch it through the off side but just about gets his bat down in time as the ball scoots low.
Outside off, pushed to the off side.
Comes forward and defends it with a slightly open bat-face, towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Short and wide outside off, HM cuts it hard and once again Nazmul dives to his right - only this time, not for the catch. Saves a boundary.
Lovely bowling, keeping it pretty straight and the batsman honest, Hamilton defends.
Full again, blocked towards point this time.
Full and outside off, more swing, Masakadza watches it closely and pushes it towards cover.
On middle, swinging in, pushed towards mid on.

DROPPED! Nazmul Islam is the culprit. The ball was hit hard but at point, you are placed for a purpose. Short and outside off, Chari cuts it through point, uppishly. Nazmul dives to his right, goes at it with two hands but cannot hang on. The batsmen take a single.
Short and outside off, slow away turn, HM looks to cut but gets a bottom edge.
Full and around off, driven towards mid off.
Landed just outside off, pushed towards point now.
Plenty of air, outside off, Hamilton drives it towards cover again.
A touch short, outside off, punched towards cover.
Full and around off, Masakadza gets a good stride forward and defends.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end.

FOUR LEG BYES! Massive shout for LBW, but the impact itself was outside leg, let alone the hitting. Full toss, way down the leg side, Chari misses his flick but the ball goes off his pads to the fine leg fence.
Similar delivery, this time it is met properly with a full face to push the ball towards mid-wicket.
Good comeback. getting the ball to swing in, landing it around middle, Brian looks to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg.

Lovely shot. Full and wide outside off, a hint of outswing, Masakadza drives it wide of mid off and almost gets a boundary. But the soggy outfield slows the ball down and the fielder is able to stop it. Three runs taken.
Landed outside off, Chari gets a good stride forward and pushes it towards cover for a single.
Full and wide outside off, a loosener, left alone.

The umpires make their way out to the middle. Bangladesh get into a team huddle. Hamilton Masakadza and Brian Chari walk out to the centre. Abu Jayed to start off proceedings. Brian to face. Here we go!

Sikandar Raza is having a chat with Ed Rainsford. Smiles on Zimbabwe getting into a dominant position after a long time and credits the entire team for the united effort. On batting today, Raza says that the aim will be to get the target around 300 - so scoring around 180-200 would be great. Adds that as the game goes on, spinners will be a lot more effective on this track. Is also surprised with the way Bangladesh opened the floodgates but is wary of the home side bouncing back. At the same time, wants his side to maintain the intensity and show the world that they can compete in Test cricket by pulling off a win.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo observes that even though 20 wickets have fallen on 2 days, the track has not deteriorated much. It has been more due to some disciplined bowling. Adds that the wicket is drier and has opened up but batting is not that difficult.

WEATHER - After bright sunshine over the weekend, heavy overcast skies welcome us on the third day. Around 2 in the morning, heavy thunderstorms hit the city and there are predictions of those continuing today as well. In fact, credit to the ground staff for drying the ground so soon, that too, without any sunshine.

Normally, Day 3 is considered to be a moving day. But this match has already got on the skates post Lunch on Sunday. Bangladesh, in totally one-day mode, just threw their wickets away, playing loose shots and have given Zimbabwe more than an upper hand in this Test. Will the visitors be able to press on the advantage? Or will the hosts roar back? Hello and a warm welcome to the third day of the first Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Sylhet.
... DAY 3, MORNING SESSION ...

The hosts were abysmal in their approach. Didn't apply themselves with the bat and never got any partnership going. They, however, are still not out of this. They will hope their spinners spin a web in the second innings and give them a reasonable target to chase. Once again all eyes will be on Taijul Islam who bagged a 6-wicket haul in the first innings. Right then, all to play for. Join us for Day 3 at 1000 local (0400 GMT) for all the action. Enjoy your Sunday and you can catch some more cricket later on in the evening when India face Windies (at 1330 GMT) and Pakistan lock horns with New Zealand (at 1600 GMT). Cheers!

The umpires have a look at the light meter and then take the bails off. That is STUMPS, Day 2! What a day for the visitors! They picked up wickets at regular intervals and ensured they get a lead of 139 runs. Their camp will be a happy one now. They will look to get as many runs as possible and then wrap up the hosts once again.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler.
Arm ball on off, skidding back in, Masakadza defends it by getting forward.
Tossed up ball on middle, Hamilton is on the front foot in defense.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched off the back foot by Hamilton but straight towards point.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler.
Floated full ball on off, Hamilton gets on the front foot in defense.
Nazmul Islam to bowl from the other end.
Another front foot defense by Chari to end the over.
Quicker and fuller on off, Brian pressed forward in defense.
Leans forward and defends it with the spin to the off side.
Flighted and full on off, it's defended off the front foot by Chari.
Flatter and shorter on middle, Masakadza goes back and punches it down to long on for a run.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended off the front foot by Hamilton.
